findings.claim: The `verification` flag — one of the three flags 18.04.01 D-04 makes mandatory on every rider item — has no mechanism anywhere in the tree, and its specified effect ('blocks the freeze even on an automatic match') is directly contradicted by 18.03.01 D-04, which says a diff `match` generates no checklist item at all.
findings.evidence: 18.04.01-technical-rider.md:50 — '| **Verification** | `trust-listing` · `require-confirmation` | Does the venue's listing data alone satisfy this, or must a human confirm? | Freeze gate (18.03.02 DT-03) |'. 18.04.01:107 — '`require-confirmation` items block the freeze even on an automatic match.' 18.04.01:134 — '| `require-confirmation` item matched automatically | Still blocks the freeze until a human at the venue confirms | "Room's data says yes — you asked for confirmation. Awaiting [venue]." |'. 18.04.01:181 — '`hard`+`unknown` and unresolved `require-confirmation` items block the freeze.' 18.04.01 D-05:68 floors EVERY power item at '`require-confirmation` on verification'. AGAINST: 18.03.01-advance-checklist.md:191 D-04 — 'A diff `match` generates **no item**. Only shortfalls, unknowns, near-matches and judgement items do'; 18.03.01:35 lists the four generating outcomes and states 'A `match` produces **no item** (D-04)'; 18.03.01 D-05/D-07 make the freeze gate 'the **hard-outstanding count** … every `hard` item not in a terminal state' over CHECKLIST items; 18.03-show-advancing-cx.md:146 R-03 — 'The freeze reads the checklist's outstanding count, not the diff's output.' 18.03.02 D-11 — 'The diff is silent and non-blocking by construction … Its only output is checklist rows and a delta notice'. Grep-verified: the strings `require-confirmation` and `trust-listing` appear ONLY in 18.04.01 — never in 18.03.01, 18.03.02 or 18.03.05 — and `verification` is not among 18.03.02 D-05's five qualifiers (`basis`, `caveats[]`, `confidence`, `severity`, `judgement-required`).
findings.failureScenario: An act's power items are floored at `require-confirmation` (18.04.01 D-05). The room's 16.02 spec states 230V/50Hz 32A, so the diff returns `match`. Per 18.03.01 D-04 the match generates no checklist item; per D-05/D-07 the freeze gate counts only checklist items; so hard-outstanding is 0 and the Producer freezes with no human at the venue having confirmed the power — the exact outcome 18.04.01:134 says is impossible. Implementer A builds the flag as inert (following 18.03.01 D-04). Implementer B invents a fifth item-generation source for matched require-confirmation rows, contradicting D-04's explicit anti-laundering rationale. Both are defensible readings and they ship different products.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a matched row with `verification: require-confirmation` generates a checklist item at all; if it does, which of 18.03.01's four generation sources it belongs to, what its severity is, and how it avoids the data-age laundering D-04 exists to prevent.
findings.shortSummary: verification flag has no mechanism; contradicts 18.03.01 D-04

findings.claim: The domain CX asserts that the post-show report, the settlement trigger, the credit and the royalty filing are all downstream of a human pressing `performed`, and die silently without it — which 18.01 D-09's system inference explicitly contradicts by design.
findings.evidence: show-production-touring-cx.md:356-359 CX-16 — 'The problem is that **all of it depends on someone pressing a button after the show ends** (18.01 DT-08) … If nobody does, both flagship loops (CX-06's cascade and CX-08's venue-truth loop) and the settlement itself die silently.' show-production-touring-cx.md:369 CX-16 §2 — '`performed` pressed → report opens (pre-filled from schedule variance) + settlement trigger fires (17) + credit created (02) + PRO royalty report fileable (10) + measured durations written back (CX-03). **Every one of these is downstream of the single press** — the domain's most consequential single point of failure.' AGAINST: 18.01-event-record-lifecycle.md:104 — 'System auto-transitions to `performed` at venue-local curfew → else scheduled set-end + 60 min → else 23:59 on the show date, and marks it **`system-inferred`, not attested** (D-09)'; 18.01 D-09:181 — 'Without inference, 18.18 and 17's settlement never trigger' (i.e. WITH inference they do); 18.18-post-show-report.md:40 Happy Path 1 — 'Show hits `performed`; the report opens pre-filled', keyed to the state, not to a press. CX-16 §5 (line 372) is itself consistent with 18.01 ('only the `performed` transition may unlock them'), so CX-16 contradicts both 18.01 and its own §5.
findings.failureScenario: Nobody presses the button after a show. Per 18.01 D-09 the record auto-transitions to `performed` (system-inferred) and the report opens and settlement is handed to 17, with the provenance grade degraded. Per CX-16 §2, nothing fires and the money never moves. A spec writer wiring triggers from the CX (the file whose job is cross-feature triggers, and which is dated 2026-07-18, later than 18.01's 2026-07-17) wires the report/settlement/credit chain to the human capture action and the inferred path becomes a dead end — settlement silently never triggers for every show where nobody pressed, which is the exact failure 18.01 D-09 was written to prevent.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the report/settlement/credit/royalty triggers fire on the `performed` state transition (including `system-inferred`) or only on a human capture action.
findings.shortSummary: CX-16 ties settlement to a human press; 18.01 D-09 infers it

findings.claim: 18.04.02's illustrative venue-facing payload prints exactly the count-of-one detail its own D-05 / DT-05 / edge case forbid.
findings.evidence: 18.04.02-hospitality-rider.md:28-29 — 'exposed to the venue as aggregated counts wherever possible: the advance carries "2 vegan, 1 gluten-free, 1 nut allergy (severe)", not four names.' AGAINST, same file: D-05:98 — 'Venue-facing aggregation has a small-count floor (count < 2 → class not detail) | Aggregation re-identifies at count of 1; the floor is what makes default-aggregate actually private'; edge case:54 — '| Aggregate count is 1, so the count re-identifies the person | Small-count disclosure defeats aggregation; below the venue-facing threshold (count < 2) the field shows "1 severe requirement — details on site" rather than the specific need in the pack |'; DT-05:78 — '"1 nut allergy" in a party of six identifies the person as surely as a name to anyone who knows the roster.' The Behavior example is the literal string DT-05 names as the failure.

findings.claim: The riders CX names an unresolved rule and points at 'Q-01 below', but the file has no Open Questions section and no Q-01 — the only dangling question pointer in the domain — leaving the severe-dietary/access buyout boundary and the authority for setting the `severe` flag with no owner and no deferral target.
findings.evidence: 18.04-riders-cx.md:96 CX-04 §1 — 'A severe allergy is arguably both — it's a dietary requirement *and* a medical need that can't be bought out (18.04.02 edge case 2). The overlap is real and **needs a resolution rule**.' 18.04-riders-cx.md:98 CX-04 §3 — 'The Producer's buyout authority stops at the medical/access line. **Where exactly that line sits is Q-01 below.**' The file ends at '## Rejected Pairs' → 'Notes for agents' → the auto-generated Related Specs block; there is no '## Open Questions' heading and no Q-row anywhere in it (verified by scanning all 70 files for Q-references against locally-defined Q-rows: this is the only dangling reference in the domain). 18.04.02 D-04 supplies the consequence ('Severe requirements (`severe` flag) cannot be silently bought out or dropped; preferences can') but no file states who may set or contest the `severe` flag, which is the line CX-04 says is open.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer building the buyout redline flow needs to know what makes a dietary item `severe` and who can assert it — the person (from their 01 profile), the Producer, or a fixed vocabulary of conditions. Nothing answers it and no tracked question routes it, so the classification authority gets invented at BE-spec time; whoever invents 'Producer sets severe' reintroduces exactly the tradeable-medical-need failure 18.04 D-03 and 18.04.03 DT-01 exist to prevent.
findings.forcedInvention: Who sets/contests the `severe` flag, and where the medical/access line sits for buyout authority.
findings.shortSummary: riders CX points at a Q-01 that does not exist

findings.claim: 'Safety-critical' is the trigger for re-opening already-advanced dates on a new rider version, but no rule, vocabulary or owner defines it — in a domain that elsewhere explicitly refuses to leave an equivalent classification to author judgement.
findings.evidence: 18.04.04-rider-templates-versioning.md:46 — '| Change is safety-critical (power spec was wrong) | Advanced dates must be re-opened, not silently left on v1 | "This change affects advanced dates — re-open them?" |'. 18.04-riders-cx.md:28 assigns the call to a human with no criteria — 'decides whether a change is safety-critical enough to re-open advanced dates'. No decision, no vocabulary and no open question in 18.04.04 (D-01..D-04, Q-01..Q-03) defines it. Contrast 18.03.05 DT-05:91 — '"Critical" can be left to the author's judgement … ❌ REJECTED — leaving criticality to the person making the change means the tired TM at T-2h under-flags exactly the change that matters most. A deterministic rule … removes the judgement call', with D-05 giving the rule.
findings.failureScenario: A rider's power spec is corrected mid-tour. Implementer A treats any change to a floored category (18.04.01 D-05: power voltage/frequency/phase) as safety-critical and force-re-opens six advanced dates, generating change-control events and venue notifications. Implementer B exposes a checkbox and the tired TM leaves it unticked, so five venues stay advanced against a spec that would destroy gear. Both are consistent with the text.
findings.forcedInvention: The rule (or the actor and the vocabulary) that classifies a rider version change as safety-critical.
findings.shortSummary: 'safety-critical' re-open trigger has no rule or owner

AGAINST: 18.03.01-advance-checklist.md:209 — '| ~~Q-02~~ | ~~What is a "hard-outstanding" item vs a soft one — who classifies, and can a venue's item block the artist's freeze?~~ | — | ✅ **RESOLVED** — see **D-06** … and **D-07** (a hard venue-side item blocks a *clean* freeze, not the freeze …)'; 18.03.01 D-07:194 — 'A `hard` **venue-side** item counts in the hard-outstanding gate — so it blocks a **clean** freeze, not the freeze … "block" means "requires an override that goes on the record"'.

findings.claim: The account-less link's write scope is simultaneously specified as working (item semantics in 18.03.01, happy path in 18.03.04) and presented as an open owner/security question that determines whether the path exists at all.
findings.evidence: SPECIFIED: 18.03.01-advance-checklist.md:60 — 'Where the answer arrives through the account-less link in an emailed sheet (18.03.04), it is `answered` and the answerer's identity is recorded as **weak**. A link answer can never self-confirm and can never `waive`.'; 18.03.01:125 edge case — '| Answer arrives via the account-less link (18.03.04) | Recorded as `answered` with **weak** identity. Cannot self-confirm, cannot `waive`.'; 18.03.04-advance-sheet.md:36 Happy Path 4 — 'Operator reads it; the QR/short link lets them answer any remaining item without an account.' OPEN: 18.03.04 Q-01:94 — 'How much can an account-less venue do via the link — read only, or answer items? The more they can do, the better the on-ramp and the larger the auth/spoofing surface. | User | `/create-prd-security`'; 18.03-show-advancing-cx.md:135 CX-06 §3 — 'Scope, expiry, and rotation are `/create-prd-security` questions (18.03.04 Q-01), and the answer determines whether CX-06 is real.'
findings.failureScenario: A spec writer must decide whether to build the link write path now. Following 18.03.01/18.03.04 they build answer-capable links and a weak-identity attestation state; following Q-01 and CX-06 they build read-only links and leave the `answered`-via-link state and its terminal-state exclusions unreachable dead code. The checklist's terminal-state vocabulary depends on which is chosen.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the weak-identity link-answer path is in scope for v1, given a sibling already specifies its state semantics.
findings.shortSummary: link write scope both specified and open

findings.claim: The one modelling decision the sub-domain admits is unresolved — whether a wedge is a plot item or a mix output — is deferred to an Open Questions section that does not exist, and is covered by no question in any file of the unit.
findings.evidence: 18.05-stage-plot-input-list-cx.md:73 CX-03 §1 — 'Wedges are the shared object. Are they plot items that mixes reference, or mix outputs that render onto the plot? Provisional answer: the mix is authoritative (a wedge exists because a mix needs it), the plot positions it. **Not yet settled — see Open Questions.**' The CX has no '## Open Questions' section. Its own notes:106 confirm the status — 'CX-03's ownership question (are wedges plot items or mix outputs?) is **the one genuinely unresolved modelling decision in this sub-domain**. It is small but it determines whether adding a mix can make an act not fit a stage.' The unit's actual questions cover other ground: index Q-01 (spatial editor), Q-02 (console export), Q-03 (versioning cadence); 18.05.01 Q-01 (editor); 18.05.02 Q-01 (console export), Q-02 (RF); 18.05.03 Q-01 (mix content depth), Q-02 (RF). None addresses wedge ownership.
findings.failureScenario: Per CX-03 §2, 'Mix added on a wedge → plot item appears → footprint changes → stage-dimension diff may newly fail', i.e. a monitor decision can make the act not fit the stage. Implementer A makes the mix authoritative and auto-creates plot items (so adding a sixth mix silently changes the footprint diffed against every venue). Implementer B makes wedges plot items that mixes reference (so adding a mix cannot change the footprint and the newly-failing diff never appears). Both are consistent with the text; the second loses a diff outcome the CX says exists.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether wedges are plot items referenced by mixes or mix outputs rendered onto the plot, and therefore whether adding a mix mutates the diffed stage footprint.

findings.claim: The roster owns the head count that drives catering, rooming and per diems, but the owning feature's contract has no touring-party vs local-labour type dimension — the requirement exists only in CX files, which themselves state that neither feature file carries it, while three downstream consumers already assume it.
findings.evidence: OWNING FEATURE (no type dimension): 18.08.01-crew-roster-call-times.md D-04:96 — 'Party size is a published input, and edits to it must be visible downstream'; Happy Path 3:41 — 'Party size (9) flows to hospitality quantities, rooming and per diems'; edge case:53 — '| Local crew hired for a date | Appears on the roster via 18.08.03 with a scoped date and access |' (no exclusion from the roll-up). THE REQUIREMENT, stated only in CX: 18.08-crew-credentials-cx.md:55 CX-02 §3 — 'A local hire is on the roster but must not be in the party-size roll-up that drives catering (18.04.02 D-01), rooming (18.12.02) and per diems (18.13.01). A naive `count(roster)` would cater for three extra stagehands and book them hotel rooms. The roster's head count needs a *type* dimension … **This is a real modelling requirement neither feature file states alone.**'; show-production-touring-cx.md:116 CX-04 §1 — 'the single most actionable modelling finding in the domain'. CONSUMERS ALREADY RELY ON IT: 18.12.01 D-02:84 — 'Party size derives from the roster, **excluding local labour**'; 18.12.02 edge case:49 — '| Local crew hired for a night | Not on the rooming list — they go home (18.08-cx CX-02) |'; 18.13-tour-finance-cx.md:75 — 'The local-labour exclusion (18.08-cx CX-02) applies here too: stagehands don't get per diems.' No open question anywhere tracks landing the dimension on the roster entity.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer builds 18.08.01 from the feature file: roster entries have person, role(s), date range, derived calls, and a party-size roll-up. Three stagehands are hired for load-in in Manchester; the roll-up returns 12; the hospitality rider caters for 12, rooming reports 12 people against 8 beds and per diems bill three extra people — reproducing the exact 'catering for the band, forgetting the crew' error class in reverse, which the CX says the type dimension exists to prevent.
findings.forcedInvention: The type dimension on the roster entry (touring party vs local labour) and which derivations exclude which type.
findings.shortSummary: roster head count lacks the local-labour type dimension

findings.claim: Whether a provisional loss mutates the manifest immediately or only on confirmation is declared unresolved with named material consequences in both directions, and no question in the unit tracks it — the unit has no live open questions at all.

Changing too early creates phantom shortfalls; too late means arriving in Leeds without a bass rig and no time to hire one. **Genuinely unresolved.**'; notes:104 — 'CX-03's timing question (provisional loss vs manifest mutation) has no good answer yet and has real consequences — a phantom shortfall or an unhired bass rig.' findings.claim: Whether a late-syncing offline receipt reopens an already-closed float reconciliation is declared unresolved and inevitable, and no question in the unit tracks it.

findings.claim: The performer view must advance without any interaction and without timecode, but nothing specifies what drives the advance — and the only stated alternative mechanism (foot control) is a device integration routed nowhere.
findings.evidence: 18.06.02-stage-ready-output.md:45 edge case — '| Performer's hands are full | No interaction can be required; **auto-advance or foot control only** | View advances on its own or not at all |'; D-02:84 — 'Zero interaction required during performance | The performer's hands are full; any view needing a tap has failed'. Q-02:92 closes the timecode route — '✅ **RESOLVED** — not by timecode … the platform is not in the playback path (18.06.03 D-01; sub-domain D-02), so it cannot know what the rig is doing in real time. Advance is therefore local to this view, and D-02 caps the permitted mechanisms to the Edge Cases row's "auto-advance or foot control only" — never a tap.' The only clock available locally is the setlist's own durations, which 18.06.01 D-02 requires to be treated as uncertain — '| Durations are estimates | Marked as such; downstream times inherit the uncertainty | "Set: ~52 min (7 of 14 songs never measured)"'. No file specifies a timer, a start trigger, or the foot-control transport (and 18.06.03's not-product routing covers MIDI/OSC only 'if 18.06.03 Q-01 lands on format-specific export').
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A builds a wall-clock timer seeded from a manually-started set time and paced by per-song estimates; on a night the band talks between songs the view is three songs ahead by mid-set, which is worse than paper for the one surface designed to be read in the dark. Implementer B reads 'or not at all' and ships no auto-advance, so the feature is a static page and the zero-interaction requirement is met trivially. Implementer C builds Bluetooth foot-pedal support, an unrouted device integration on a PWA.
findings.forcedInvention: What clock drives auto-advance and what starts it; whether foot-control hardware is in scope.
findings.shortSummary: performer-view auto-advance has no specified clock or trigger
